mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede statistically significant negative returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth expectations for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 decline triggers but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and returns is not significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1 standard deviation within the same month signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases > 1 std dev AND PAYEMS decreases > 1 std dev in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the joint trigger does not precede statistically significant negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1.0% AND HOUST monthly change < -1.0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during co-occurring GDPC1 and HOUST declines (t-test p > 0.10), or the joint trigger is not followed by a market drop in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points within a single month, in the absence of a concurrent recession signal (UNRATE > 5%), signals aggressive tightening that outweighs growth headwinds, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipation of future easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered months, or the trigger does not precede statistically significant positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations for consumer-facing S&P 500 firms and leads to positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during sustained GDPC1 recoveries (t-test p > 0.10), or the always-on signal fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of episodes.
